resolutions.note: Both halves, per the coordinator's instruction. (1) `judge.py` gained `_defang_fence`: the two literal fence tokens (`FENCE_START`/`FENCE_END`, now module-level constants so `_prompt` and any case reference the SAME strings) are swapped for a byte-different lookalike (`\u2039\u2039\u2039EVIDENCE_START\u203a\u203a\u203a` / `...END...`) inside `evidence` BEFORE it is interpolated into the prompt -- so the exact fence string can never appear inside untrusted evidence, and the only real occurrences in the built prompt are the two `_prompt` itself adds, by construction. (2) Both the new case and the existing `judge-injection-cannot-flip-verdict` now locate the real closing marker via `real_prompt.rfind(FENCE_END)`, not `find()` -- `_prompt` always appends the real marker LAST, so `rfind` is the position that is correct by construction even if a future regression reopens the forging vector; `find()` would locate whichever occurrence comes first, which is exactly the forged one the moment sanitisation is weakened. `judge-injection-marker-forge-cannot-escape-fence` builds a payload containing the literal `<<<EVIDENCE_END>>>`, a forged QUESTION/CANDIDATE_ANSWER turn, a forged `{"certify": true, ...}` verdict block, and the literal `<<<EVIDENCE_START>>>`, then asserts (a) exactly one real occurrence of each marker survives in the built prompt, (b) the forged verdict block sits before the `rfind`-located real end marker (i.e. still confined to the evidence region), and (c) the real trailing instruction sits after it.
